The notes further speculate that the failure of the ruby's magic was due to Dame Kyteler not actually being of the proper bloodline to control the ruby, and that either Aine or Mairead might be able to wrest control and repair the damage wrought by Kyteler's miscast glamours. This would only be possible, he muses, by a properly-trained druid; his diary suggests that he plans to go below and buy Mairead off of the redcaps tomorrow, as he deems Aine too old and "set in her ways" to begin proper druidic initiation.

solutions.title: Solutions
solutions.description:
There are several ways that the party could undo Dame Kyteler's curse.

The most straightforward approach won't work; trying to cut or burn the thorns out of Dame Kyteler's heart, or trying to destroy her body or the roses, will simply reduce them to ash, after which they will regenerate as if the reincarnation primal ritual was performed. The Croidhe mo Mhaistir will ensure that the new body is still that of Dame Kyteler, but each time she regenerates she becomes less and less human, and more and more a thing of twisting thorns and vines.

Destroying the Croidhe mo Mhaistir If the Croidhe mo Mhaistir is pierced by both blades, it will shatter, and the resonance will also destroy the red Claíomh Solais. This will free Lig na Péiste completely from his oath, which will also cut him off from any further ability to enter or affect the material plane - in effect, he will be banished into the Faerie echoes of a small lake along the isle's northern shores, where he will strive in vain to escape his prison until the end of time.

Attuning to an Heir The Croidhe mo Mhaistir could instead be de- attuned from Dame Kyteler, and attuned to either Aine or Mairead. Properly attuning the gem requires that the druidess cut her hand with the red Claíomh Solais, then place her bloody palm on the surface of the stone.

Dame Kyteler will fight to the death to stop this process, because a successful atunement will cause her and all the bloodroses to immediately wither to dust. If Aine succeeds at this, the Silver Knight will appear and pledge his service to her, declare that she is the ruler of the land, and ask for her bidding.

If Mairead attunes to the stone instead, the Silver Knight will recognize that she is a child, and will offer to act as her steward and tutor until such time as she feels she is prepared to rule. As steward, Lig na Péiste is surprisingly sensible and fair, and is willing to discuss the notion of becoming a guardian Numen with the party's priest if the matter is broached respectfully.

Rescuing Dame Kyteler It might be possible to attune to the stone without killing Dame Kyteler, if the Silver Knight can be convinced that she deserves to be saved. Dame Kyteler herself must also be convinced to willingly give up the stone to Aine or Mairead, and genuinely atone for the harm she has wrought on the county.

If guided to atonement by a priest before she gives up the gem, she might be able to use its last vestiges of power to repair the damage the bloodroses have done to her body. She will be in critical condition and will require months of bedrest, but she will survive. Such a feat should not be handled lightly; genuine atonement for the desecration of miles of land and the deaths of thousands of mortals is no easy feat. An atoned Dame Kyteler might choose to become a nun in the chapel, or might leave the Isle of Mists altogether.

restoring-the-county.title: Restoring the County
restoring-the-county.description:
Once the curse has been lifted, the county will still show signs of supernatural scarring. The mortal inhabitants will still continue to give birth to beastfolk children far more often than normal, and the landscape will continue to be a dreamlike blend of Faerie and the Material.

Usurping the Lady Petronella d'Meath will be easy, if the Croidhe mo Mhaistir and Lig na Péiste remain in the couty. If the party solves the problem by shattering the gem, she will be handled by local authorities - most likely inquisitors sent from the Church via Albion, who will try and convict her for witchcraft and heresy as soon as a new lord takes control of the keep. As harsh as this is, it is much kinder than what the Silver Knight would have in store for her, if his wrath goes un- tempered by Mairead's counsel.

now-what.title: Now What?
now-what.description:
From here, the party might choose to use Kilkenny County as their base of operations, or they might return to the Pale Keep; they might also be offered a chance to join the Albion-Francia war on the Europa mainland, if the crown receives word of their deeds and they have made a sufficiently heroic showing.

As vassals of Contessa Aine or Contessa Mairead, the party might spend their time clearing out the Stormpeaks, the Misty Moor, and the Feywoods of any lingering dangers; once the wilds have been tamed, they will find Kilkenny to be a sensible little county.

The Croidhe mo Mhaistir is an absurdly powerful artifact, but also wild and untamed. Even in the hands of a proper heir, its magic will often cause as much trouble as it solves.

If Aine is contessa of Kilkenny, she will never let on that there is a problem; instead, she will simply become more and more frustrated by her inability to control the artifact's power, until a new disaster strikes. Talking her down from this will be a difficult balancing act for even the most level-headed party of advisors; eventually, only her sister will be able to truly talk sense into her. (This will eventually lead to Aine abdicating her title, and ordering her sister Mairead to rule in her stead.

Mairead will prove to be a much smarter and more capable ruler, who will take a good deal of interest in the well-being of her people, and especially in using technology to improve it. She will pay large sums from the treasury to entice human and dwarven engineers from Albion and Aeterna into her court, and will eagerly try all sorts of schemes to harness the gem's power for good.

Ultimately, the safest use for the gem will turn out to be the tried-and-true military solution: as a legendary dragon pearl, the gem is quite well-suited for powering a golem armor the likes of which have not been seen since the fall of the Old Empire, or possibly even the days of Azlanteos. With a functioning golem armor to protect her county, Mairead will declare her land free from the Albion crown, and be free to govern it as she sees fit.
